citations.claim: just before impact the body moves right at ~38.89 m/s with total energy ~814 J (baseline)
after the wall bounce in step 7 the x-velocity magnitude grew from 38.89 to 41.33 despite e=0.91, showing super-elastic impulse
first energy_bound violation at step 7: total energy rose to ~911.9 J with no controller work

counterfactual.change: Set restitution e from 0.91279 to 0.0, keeping all else identical; inelastic impact removes the spurious energy gain and the scenario passes.

explanation: High-speed (~39 m/s) impact against thin (0.1 wide) wall with e~0.91 produces a super-elastic bounce: outgoing speed 41.34 exceeds incoming 38.90, so kinetic energy rises from ~814 J to ~911.9 J with zero controller work. Likely cause is restitution impulse and/or positional correction being applied repeatedly across many substeps (21-22 substeps in steps 6-7) or overshooting, effectively yielding e>1.
vision_note: A blue circle moves rightward toward the top tip of a thin vertical wall over steps 4 to 5 and makes contact by step 6. In step 7 it remains at the wall tip after impact, with no visible tunneling through or deep penetration of the wall.
